name: gnomon
description: Deterministic coding agent harness — repo-scoped config, content-hashed surface

scripts.setup: pnpm install && pnpm run build:native && pnpm run link:global
scripts.build:native:
if command -v cargo >/dev/null 2>&1; then cargo build --release --workspace --bins; else printf '
  cargo not found - SKIPPING the native build (this is not an error).
  Works without it:  gnomon launch | prompt | task | init
  Needs it:          gnomon surface | apply | session, and the Rust tests
  To get it:         curl https://sh.rustup.rs -sSf | sh   (https://rustup.rs)
                     then re-run: pnpm run build:native
  Or unpack a release archive and export GNOMON_BIN_OVERRIDE at it -
  see GETTING_STARTED.md, "Prebuilt binaries".

'; fi
scripts.link:global:
cd packages/gnomon-cli && { pnpm link --global || true; }; if command -v gnomon >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '
  gnomon is on PATH: %s

' "$(command -v gnomon)"; else printf '
  FAILED: gnomon is NOT on PATH after `pnpm link --global`.

  pnpm writes the shim into its global bin directory, which is $PNPM_HOME.
  With PNPM_HOME unset - the default state after `corepack enable pnpm` -
  pnpm links the package, writes no shim on PATH, prints only
  "WARN ... has no binaries", and exits 0. Measured with pnpm 9.0.0 on
  2026-09-02. That warning is the failure, not a note.

  Fix it once:
      pnpm setup             # sets PNPM_HOME and puts it on PATH in your shell rc
      exec $SHELL            # or just open a new terminal
      pnpm run link:global   # re-run this step

  Or skip the global link and use the launcher in this checkout - same
  program, no PATH change:
      ./gnomon launch

' >&2; exit 1; fi
